items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1989-08-13
items.q: most of them went up north, like Perez and all the people who led bands in the district were gone.

ctx.x: Yeah, okay, in that area. Yeah.

Right. Well, of course, the cabaret business was about shot in the rest of the city because people were going down to the district for entertainment, for the most part. And a lot of the musicians just packed up and left town. The real exodus of musicians started in 1913, not in 1917 when the district was closed. Right. Legally. And so most of them went up north, like Perez and all the people who led bands in the district were gone. How long was the shutdown? Well, the shutdown lasted, I mean, until the district…
Wait, so between 1913 and 1970? Yeah, no cabaret music. There was no, there were no live bands and people?
